Trigger a new run of a pipeline

## Usage

`circleci pipeline run [flags]`

## Flags

| Flag                     | Description                                                                       |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-b, --branch string`    | Branch to run (defaults to the checkout's current branch)                         |
| `--definition string`    | Pipeline definition name; needed when the project has several                     |
| `--definition-id string` | Pipeline definition UUID, instead of --definition                                 |
| `--jq string`            | Process values from the response using jq syntax (see `circleci help formatting`) |
| `--json`                 | Output as JSON                                                                    |
| `--param stringArray`    | Pipeline parameter as key=value (repeatable)                                      |
| `--project string`       | Project slug (e.g. gh/org/repo); defaults to git remote                           |
| `-t, --tag string`       | Tag to run, instead of --branch                                                   |

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Examples

- Trigger a run on the current branch, picking the pipeline from a menu: 
  `circleci pipeline run`
- Trigger a pipeline, selected by name, on a branch: 
  `circleci pipeline run --project gh/myorg/myrepo --definition main-pipeline --branch main`
- Trigger on a tag with parameters: 
  `circleci pipeline run --project gh/myorg/myrepo --definition-id 2338d0ae-5541-4bbf-88a2-55e9f7281f80 --tag v1.2.3 --param deploy_env=staging`
- Output as JSON for scripting: 
  `circleci pipeline run --definition main-pipeline --json`

## Details

Trigger a run of a project's pipeline; works for OAuth, GitHub App and GitLab
projects. Same as 'circleci run trigger'. A project with several pipelines
needs --definition, which a terminal prompts for.

JSON fields: id, pipeline_id, project_id, created_at, branch, tag
